scenario.name: Microsoft Threat Intel & CISA ED 24-02 — Midnight Blizzard Legacy OAuth Test Application & Exchange Online EWS Audit
scenario.overview: Picture an international border crossing checkpoint with glass passport inspection booths, zig-zag queue stanchions, an X-ray luggage conveyor belt, and a striped crossing barrier. Approaching the international border crossing, a traveler steps up to the glass passport booth carrying a travel booklet with a subtly altered entry stamp. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the luggage x-ray belt & barrier in tiny disguised batches, then quietly copies a trusted access pass from the border customs officer's station. A secondary customs officer cross-checks the border passport registry and catches a stamp serial number that was never issued by that embassy. In this scenario (T1110.003, Microsoft Threat Intel & CISA ED 24-02, Midnight Blizzard Legacy OAuth Test Application & Exchange Online EWS Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: low-Volume Residential Proxy Password Spray, then service Principal Credential Addition, then oAuth Bearer Token EWS Mailbox Sync. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Low-Volume Residential Proxy Password Spray, then Service Principal Credential Addition, then OAuth Bearer Token EWS Mailbox Sync, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1110.003 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 3: OAuth Bearer Token EWS Mailbox Sync & MailItemsAccessed Telemetry
stages.subtitle: Collection (T1114.002 - Remote Email Collection)
stages.description: Rolling luggage smoothly off the X-ray conveyor into the secure arrival hall, the traveler crosses the border wearing an official-looking entry clearance. In this final step inside the border control, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the border customs officer's station until the customs passport registry catches the mismatch. Authenticating solely with OAuth 2.0 client_credentials tokens from the malicious Service Principal, the actor queries Exchange Web Services (EWS) without interactive user sign-ins, generating MailItemsAccessed events in the Microsoft Purview Unified Audit Log (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with AuditOperation=MailItemsAccessed, ProtocolWorkload=Exchange Web Services , EWS, OAuthClientAppId=a8f4c210-1122-4433-9988-776655443322 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations MailItemsAccessed -FreeText "Legacy-OAuth-Test-App" (which invokes Microsoft 365 Exchange Online / Graph API operations to silently read victim mailbox items , MailItemsAccessed or create hidden inbox forwa so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1114.002 during "OAuth Bearer Token EWS Mailbox Sync & MailItemsAccessed Telemetry" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact OfficeActivity | where Operation == "MailItemsAccessed" and ClientAppId == "a8f4c210-1122-4433-9988-776655443322" runs (which invokes Microsoft 365 Exchange Online / Graph API operations to silently read victim mailbox items , MailItemsAccessed or create hidden inbox forwa so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1114.002 during "OAuth Bearer Token EWS Mailbox Sync & MailItemsAccessed Telemetry" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ EWS SyncFolderItems via OAuth Application Token (MailItemsAccessed) / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 Entra ID Sign-In & OAuth Consent API) to Node ④ (#4 Legacy Test OAuth App Principal), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Exchange Online EWS Mailboxes).

keySpecs.value: Enforce Exchange Online Application Access Policies (New-ApplicationAccessPolicy) to restrict EWS/Graph application tokens to explicitly scoped security groups and revoke unauthorized OAuth Service Principals.
